result.title: Fine-Grained Analysis of Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Learning via Algorithmic Stability
result.summary: Understanding catastrophic forgetting, in which learning new tasks degrades performance on previously learned tasks, remains a fundamental challenge in continual learning (CL). Existing theoretical analyses often rely on specific model or task structures and offer limited insight into how iterative optimization affects forgetting. To address this gap, we develop an algorithmic stability framework for expected population forgetting under SGD without prescribing a particular model architecture. Specifically, we decompose forgetting into intra-task and cross-task generalization gaps and empirical forgetting. To bound the generalization gaps, we track how a sample perturbation affects updates within a task and propagates through subsequent tasks. We consider constant, intra-task decaying, and continuously decaying learning-rate schedules. Comparing the two decaying schedules allows us to characterize how restarting learning-rate decay at task boundaries affects the propagation of historical sample perturbations. For empirical forgetting, we derive bounds for all three schedules by retaining cumulative gradient alignment along the optimization trajectory, without requiring convexity. Combining these results yields upper bounds on expected forgetting that capture the effects of training set size, the number of updates per task, the total number of tasks, learning-rate schedules, and cumulative gradient alignment. Finally, we conduct experiments on Split CIFAR-100 and Split MiniImageNet to examine the empirical implications of our theoretical findings.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出不依赖特定模型结构的算法稳定性框架，把 SGD 下的期望遗忘分解为任务内与跨任务泛化差距及经验遗忘，追踪样本扰动在后续任务更新中的传播，并在常数、任务内衰减和持续衰减三种学习率下推导遗忘上界，最后在 Split CIFAR-100 与 Split MiniImageNet 上做验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其扰动传播与任务边界处学习率重启的分析，可能为「新任务训练如何冲刷已有 latent 推理状态」「视觉证据扰动在多步更新中的残留」提供可核查的理论工具，而非直接研究 LVR。
